issues.description: The template's ArrayHelpers defines a method named appendElement(...), but other template classes (e.g., Stock) call ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). The solution uses addElementToArray(...). This name/signature mismatch in the template will cause compilation errors and prevents students from building or running the starter project.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent. Rename the method in the template ArrayHelpers from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...), matching the calls in Stock.java and the solution, or update Stock and other call sites to use appendElement(...). Prefer renaming ArrayHelpers in the template to addElementToArray(...) to align with the solution and other template code.

issues.description: The helper method that adds an element to an array is referenced with different identifiers across artifacts. The template Stock class calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...), and the solution's ArrayHelpers defines addElementToArray(...), but the template's ArrayHelpers defines the method as appendElement(...). This mismatch will cause compilation errors and creates unnecessary mapping confusion for students who must reconcile two different method names for the exact same utility operation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name for appending/adding an element to an array across template and solution. Either rename the template ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) or change Stock and other callers to use appendElement(...). Prefer aligning to addElementToArray(...) (as used in the solution) to avoid student confusion and compilation errors.
